methods.text: Describe the work out loud while doing it and note each hesitation.
Make the worst possible version on purpose, then list what it teaches.
Fix the order of reading before choosing any sizes.
Ask a user to sort the parts into piles, then follow their piles.
Write the first question a skeptic will ask and answer it on the first screen.
Keep a log of every decision with one reason, and reread it at the end.
Change one variable at a time and record the effect of each change.
Give every part a removal date unless it earns its place by then.

constraints.text: The core result works with scripts turned off.
Shows no more than three result numbers at once.

tasks.text: Customer loss calculator: customer count, monthly loss rate, and average monthly value give revenue lost over 12 months and the value of cutting the rate by one point.
Price change tester: current price, volume, and a new price give the revenue at the new price and the volume drop that would cancel the gain.
Contract term comparer: monthly and annual terms with discount and exit fee give the total cost of staying 6, 12, or 24 months under each.
Rework cost calculator: errors per 100 cases, cases per month, and cost to fix each give the monthly rework cost and the saving from halving errors.
Sign-off planner: the roles that must approve and the days each takes give the earliest decision date and the slowest approval step.
Tool overlap finder: the tools the buyer pays for and the jobs each does give the jobs covered twice and the monthly spend on overlap.

methods: Design the error and empty states first.
List the assumptions in the brief and check each one.
Make it work in black and white before adding color.
Take the conventions of a genre and break exactly one.
Write the copy before the layout.
Scope the work to what fits in one day.
constraints: Under 100 words of fixed text on the page.
tasks: Cost-of-inaction calculator: the buyer's current volumes and rates give what the problem costs per month and per year, with each step of the sum shown.
Readiness scorecard: twelve yes-or-no questions give a score out of 100, the three weakest areas, and one next step for each.
Benchmark checker: the buyer's own figures sit next to typical ranges they can edit, with each gap marked ahead, level, or behind.
Leak finder: a funnel of stages with counts gives the stage that loses the most and what fixing half of that loss would be worth.
Time-back calculator: weekly hours on manual tasks and an hourly cost give the hours and money an automated step would return.
Before-and-after map: today's process as a list of steps becomes a side-by-side view marking the steps that could be removed or automated.
